transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-02
Time: 15:00-15:42 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Martin (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood CSM), Jordan Lee (Kestrel Head Procurement), Marta Ruiz (Kestrel InfoSec), Devon Park (Platform), Laila Chen (Legal), Ethan Moore (SRE)

Summary (auto): quick procurement/infosec gate: verify MSA/DPA redlines, confirm KMS/egress and SOC2, pricing acceptance path, pilot scoping and technical deep dive.

[00:00] Alex Martin: alright, good afternoon everyone thanks for making time, I think we have about 40 minutes, quick intros then jump to the MSA points and the technical acceptance items.
[00:20] Jordan Lee: hey, Jordan here, procurement — we just want to make sure the path for approval is clear. timeline is tight, expecting purchasing committee next Wednesday.
[00:28] Marta Ruiz: Marta from InfoSec, hi. we need KMS details, encryption at rest and transit, and an audit log flow.
[00:35] Priya Desai: hi all, Priya from Redwood infra, I'll run through technical constraints and the dedicated capacity options.
[00:42] Devon Park: Devon, platform, we'll want to run a small pilot and do a latency bench. our main concerns are tail latency and egress cost.

[01:05] Alex Martin: great, top-level — contract wise Kestrel asked for a few MSA redline points last week: data residency clause, audit access, and indemnity carve-outs. Laila, can you confirm which are blockers for you?
[01:20] Laila Chen: yes, indemnity is sticky; pricing model also needs clarity around egress fees and kms keying costs. we need the DPA to explicitly state that logs are retained for 90 days and explain deletion processes.
[01:35] Samir Patel: on the compliance front we have our SOC2 type II and a recent pen test; I'll attach both. also we support customer-managed keys via our KMS integration, for private deployments.

[02:10] Marta Ruiz: the KMS bit — is that supported for Hosted or only Dedicated/Private? we can't have keys we don't control in production.
[02:22] Priya Desai: you can do customer-managed keys in Redwood Private (VPC) and Dedicated with KMS integration; hosted option by default uses Redwood-managed keys but we offer an SME path for key escrow, however that's more complex. (some audio fade, background)
[02:45] Speaker 1: um, sorry can you repeat the difference between Dedicated and Private.
[02:50] Alex Martin: sure — Dedicated is reserved GPU pools in our cloud, shared control plane but isolated capacity; Private is customer-managed control plane in your VPC or on-prem, so you get full key control. Dedicated gives predictable throughput with SLAs, Private gives more control for regs.

[03:30] Jordan Lee: procurement will push back on price if egress fees or per-token add-ons are ambiguous. we need a clean quote: base monthly for dedicated capacity plus per-token tiers.
[03:45] Alex Martin: understood. we can provide a pricing ladder — baseline reserved nodes price, plus burst credit and per-token charges for inference and embeddings. Priya will include suggested batching/quantization to reduce unit cost.

[04:10] Devon Park: performance: our workload is chatty — 1k users, median seq len 120 tokens, 95th is 680. ephemeral context, but we also do reranking. how does KV cache affect cost?
[04:28] Priya Desai: we do KV cache and prefix caching; if you can pin prompts or reuse context we see big reductions. on dedicated you get more efficient KV caching; on-hosted there is still prefix cache but less control. note transcription: KV "cash" sometimes in older notes.

[05:05] Marta Ruiz: on audit logs — we need access to per-request metadata, query text retention controls, and the ability to export logs to our SIEM. is that available?
[05:18] Samir Patel: yes, export to your S3 or SIEM is supported; we have route-level logging and token-level cost breakdowns in the Console. will attach screenshot of the Console export options.

[06:00] Laila Chen: one more legal item — we require a limited subprocessor list and a flow for notification within 48 hours of any security incident. can you commit to that?
[06:12] Alex Martin: standard is 72 hours for incident notification in our MSA; we can discuss 48 hours as an addendum — we'll propose concrete language in the redline.

[06:45] Jordan Lee: for procurement gate we also need acceptance criteria for the pilot — what defines success?
[06:55] Priya Desai: from an SE perspective: throughput > X qps on N dedicated nodes, p95 latency under 350ms for the typical prompt mix, and model-output quality stable against your eval set. we'll propose a checklist.

[07:30] Devon Park: is the latency number realistic? 350ms p95 for 680 tokens seems optimistic.
[07:38] Priya Desai: fair — the 350ms is for median lengths; for long sequences p95 will increase. for long form we recommend a larger ded pool or model quantization. we'll share a table mapping sequence length to expected latency per model variant.

[08:12] Ethan Moore: another operational ask — can we run the pilot in our eu-west region to satisfy residency?
[08:20] Alex Martin: yes eu-west is supported, we can pin the pilot to the region. for Private deployments we can also do on-prem if needed but that adds lead time.

[09:00] Marta Ruiz: encryption in transit — do you support mTLS and SAML-based SSO for service accounts?
[09:08] Priya Desai: yes TLS+ mTLS for inter-service is supported, and SAML/SSO for user access; for service-to-service you can use client certs or token-based auth.

[09:45] Jordan Lee: what about auditability — we need immutable logs for 12 months for the pilot. is that feasible?
[09:52] Samir Patel: default retention is 90 days but we have add-on retention to 12 months; I'll price that in the attachment.

[10:20] Laila Chen: DPA question — do you permit subprocessor transparency? we need a list of subprocessors and the right to audit.
[10:30] Alex Martin: yes we publish a subprocessor list and can include a clause for audit rights subject to NDA; I'll include that in the redline.

[11:00] Jordan Lee: can we talk about fallback policies — if Dedicated capacity is saturated what's automated fallback?
[11:10] Priya Desai: we have smart routing; we can fallback to a lower-cost compatible model or route to another region; customer can set policy: strict (fail) vs graceful (fallback) and we can configure automatic canaries and rollbacks.

[12:00] Devon Park: curious about cost controls — can we cap daily spend and enforce hard limits?
[12:10] Alex Martin: yes you can set quotas per token and per route; Console supports alerting and hard limits to throttle.

[12:45] Jordan Lee: procurement wants a single number for the approval packet — what would you recommend we present?
[12:52] Alex Martin: for approval present two lanes: conservative pilot lane (1 reserved node, 3-week pilot, estimated $X/month + egress) and expansion lane with three reserved nodes and cost per million tokens for production. we'll send a pricing sheet.

[13:40] Marta Ruiz: on the security docs — please share your pen test artifacts, SOC2 scope doc, and data flow diagrams.
[13:48] Samir Patel: yes will attach links: [link: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf], [link: redwood-pen-test-summary.pdf], [link: redwood-dataflow-diagram.png].

[14:20] Laila Chen: one more, KMS key rotation — how do we coordinate rotating customer keys without downtime?
[14:30] Priya Desai: we support key rotation with key aliases, and for private deployments you can rotate at will; we'll share playbook (we call it key swap window) and recommended cadence.

[15:00] (discussion shifts to pricing specifics — audio overlap)
[15:10] Alex Martin: I'll summarise pricing: reserved capacity monthly fee, per-token for embeddings/generation, optional retention and egress add-ons, plus a one-time onboarding fee if Private deployment. We'll send a formal quote.

[16:05] Jordan Lee: what about competitive differentiation — one of our teams asked about CloudRunAI offering a lower per-token price but no dedicated capacity SLA. why Redwood?
[16:15] Alex Martin: Redwood's value is production SLOs, consistent performance, and unified tooling across hosted/dedicated/private — so you don't rebuild when you move to private. plus the Optimize toolkit to reduce per-token cost.

[17:00] Devon Park: how long to stand up Dedicated pilot?
[17:06] Priya Desai: typically 3-7 business days once the compute is provisioned and network peering is complete; Private on-prem typically 4-8 weeks.

[17:35] Ethan Moore: network peering — will we need static IP ranges for outbound egress?
[17:42] Priya Desai: yes we publish egress IP ranges for peering; for Private deployments you control egress.

[18:10] Laila Chen: legal acceptance: if you provide the MSA+DPA redline we'll route it through our counsel; timeline is ~five business days for an initial pass.

[19:00] Alex Martin: ok recap before we close — action items: we'll circulate the redlines and security artifacts, Redwood provides pricing ladder and pilot acceptance checklist, customer provides traffic profile and approver list. schedule deep technical run-through next week.

[19:22] Jordan Lee: sounds good. one ask — can you include an explicit rollback SLA in the pilot plan?
[19:30] Priya Desai: yes we'll include rollback windows and canary config in the runbook.

[20:00] Alex Martin: great, thanks everyone. I'll follow up with calendar invites for the tech deep dive and send the doc bundle.
[20:10] Samir Patel: noted, I'll upload the SOC2 and pen test to the ticket.

[20:25] (meeting ends, brief small talk)

Notes about transcript: transcription has occasional mis-attributions (Speaker 1) and minor mis-words (KV cash vs KV cache). Shared artifacts: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (link sent), redwood-pen-test-summary.pdf (link sent), dedicated-perf-runbook.xlsx (to be attached).

End of transcript.
